walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Performance — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many bones are in the adult human skeleton?

options: Elbow
Knee
Hip
Wrist

mcqs.q: What type of joint is the knee?
options: Second class.
A hinge joint.
A pivot joint.
A ball and socket joint.

mcqs.q: According to the inverted-U hypothesis, when is performance best?
options: When arousal is at minimum.
When arousal is at maximum.
A pivot joint.
At an optimal moderate level of arousal.

mcqs.q: Most movements in the human body use which class of lever?
options: First class.
A pivot joint.
Second class.
Third class.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Axial skeleton”?
options: Tough connective tissue joining bone to bone, stabilising joints.
Where two or more bones meet; classified by type and movement.
Skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum; protects vital organs.
Freely movable joint with synovial fluid; e.g., hinge (elbow), ball-and-socket (hip).
